claims.subject: Layouts
claims.text: Layouts is the single container that stitches every enabled layout child into one flat physical address space, shared by all layers.

claims.subject: LayoutBase
claims.text: A layout is a coordinate iterator: it reports how many lights it has and emits each light's physical index with an (x, y, z) position, and it owns no mapping table.

claims.subject: LayoutBase::lightCount
claims.text: A layout's count comes from the same walk as its placement (run without a sink), so lightCount and placeLights cannot disagree.

claims.subject: CoordSink
claims.text: Layouts emit through a function-pointer sink (callback, gap callback, context) instead of std::function or a returned vector, so placement allocates nothing and the same walk serves counting, bounding-box and LUT passes.

claims.subject: CoordSink::blackPixel
claims.text: A gap light (blackPixel) is a physical wire slot that stays dark; it goes to blackCb, or falls back to cb when the consumer supplies none.

claims.subject: LightEmitter
claims.text: LightEmitter is the running physical index a layout emits through; it stops at the light limit, counts when it has no sink, and lets a layout append whole sub-layouts via place().

claims.subject: LightEmitter::place
claims.text: place() relays a part layout's callbacks, adding the running offset to its indices and the shift to its coordinates, then advances idx by the part's lightCount even when there is no sink.

claims.subject: LayoutBase::hasBlackPixels
claims.text: A layout holding slots dark must report hasBlackPixels, because that switches off the dense identity fast path, whose one-to-one map would otherwise light the gap.

claims.subject: LayoutBase::affectsPrepare
claims.text: Every layout control change rebuilds the whole pipeline, since each one changes the light count or order.

claims.subject: LayoutBase::clampedCount
claims.text: Light counts are computed in a wider integer and clamped to nrOfLightsType's maximum, so an oversized layout clamps instead of wrapping.

claims.subject: LayoutBase wiring controls
claims.text: Wiring controls (reversed, serpentine, axis order) change only the order lights are emitted, never a light's coordinate, because the emission order is what the driver's index means.

claims.subject: Layouts::totalLightCount
claims.text: totalLightCount sums the enabled children, returns 0 when the container itself is disabled, and caps the total at maxLights(); it sizes both layer and output buffers.

claims.subject: Layouts::maxLights
claims.text: Safe mode caps placement at 1024 lights because a layout too large for memory would crash the device at every boot.

claims.subject: Layouts::placeLights
claims.text: Disabling or reordering a layout shifts the physical indices of every later layout, which moves Art-Net universe assignments.

claims.subject: Layouts::prepare
claims.text: prepare runs one placeLights pass to find the bounding box (max coordinate plus one per axis, gaps included) and writes 'N lights · WxHxD' to the status line, flagging a warning when the count is 0.

claims.subject: Layouts one light type
claims.text: Each layout describes one light type (LED strips or par lights); the model is one light type per layout, never mixed within a single layout.

claims.subject: LayoutBase::dimensions
claims.text: A layout's dimensions() is advisory (UI chip only); nothing in the render path reads it, so declaring the wrong Dim cannot break a render.

claims.subject: GridLayout
claims.text: GridLayout is the dense 1D/2D/3D grid wired x fastest, then y, then z, with an optional serpentine that reverses every odd row.

claims.subject: GridLayout::serpentine
claims.text: Serpentine changes only the index-to-position order, which is what makes the layout's map non-identity and forces a real LUT.

claims.subject: PanelLayout
claims.text: PanelLayout is the general 2D matrix panel with a choice of first axis, direction per axis and serpentine; GridLayout is its simple case.

claims.subject: PanelsLayout
claims.text: PanelsLayout tiles a video wall with two nested PanelLayout objects: an outer one walks the grid of panels and at each cell places the inner panel offset to its tile.

claims.subject: GridBlacksLayout
claims.text: GridBlacksLayout is a grid with dark columns that stay wire positions the driver clocks but receive no color, for sealed panels or slat walls.

claims.subject: GridBlacksLayout::placeLights
claims.text: Dark columns are decided at the emit site from the true x coordinate, never re-derived from an index, so a column stays dark whichever way a serpentine row enters it.

claims.subject: WheelLayout
claims.text: WheelLayout places spokes radiating from a hub using byte angles (256 per turn) and the sin8/cos8 tables, so placement is integer-only.

claims.subject: WheelLayout sparse
claims.text: A wheel is sparse: only spoke positions hold lights, so box cells between spokes have no light and the layer needs a non-identity LUT for it.

claims.subject: RingLayout / CarLightsLayout / Rings241Layout
claims.text: Composite layouts are built from RingLayout objects with their own centers and placed through LightEmitter::place, so a lamp is drawn by the same layout a user adds as a Ring.

claims.subject: TubesLayout
claims.text: TubesLayout places each tube as a SingleColumnLayout object, the whole of one tube before the next.

claims.subject: SphereLayout
claims.text: SphereLayout selects lattice points whose distance from the center rounds to the radius, comparing squared integer distances so no light costs a square root, with one walk shared by count and emit.

claims.subject: SpiralLayout
claims.text: SpiralLayout winds lights up a cone whose radius falls linearly to zero while the winding rate stays the base's, packing tightly at the base and opening toward the tip.

claims.subject: CubeLayout
claims.text: CubeLayout fills a width x height x depth box with a strip path set by axis order, per-axis direction and per-axis snake; it is the 3D form of PanelLayout.

claims.subject: HumanSizedCubeLayout
claims.text: HumanSizedCubeLayout is a walk-in cube of five LED curtains (front, back, top, left, right), open at the bottom.

claims.subject: SingleRowLayout / SingleColumnLayout
claims.text: SingleRowLayout and SingleColumnLayout are the 1D strips laid along x at a fixed y and along y at a fixed x.

claims.subject: TorontoBarGourdsLayout
claims.text: TorontoBarGourdsLayout places 24 gourds, each lit at one of three granularities (one light per gourd, per side, or per LED).

claims.subject: Layer
claims.text: A Layer owns a buffer sized to its logical box, a MappingLUT onto physical positions, and two child lists (effects that write the buffer, modifiers that reshape it).

claims.subject: Layer::prepare
claims.text: The cold path computes the physical box from one placeLights pass, calls rebuildLUT, zeroes the buffer, sizes the live scratch and sets the 'WxHxD' status, and applyState then recurses to the effects, which allocate against the new LUT.

claims.subject: Layer::prepare empty path
claims.text: With no layouts or zero lights the layer frees its LUT and buffer together, because a stale LUT beside a zero-byte buffer makes blendMap fault.

claims.subject: Layer::tick
claims.text: Each frame the layer applies the collected fade, ticks every enabled effect (extruding its output), ticks the modifiers, rebuilds once if any asked, and otherwise runs the live pass only when a live modifier exists.

claims.subject: Layer::tick child iteration
claims.text: Layer::tick iterates and gates its children itself rather than through the Scheduler, so it checks role and enabled per child and does not chain to MoonModule::tick.

claims.subject: Layer::tick empty grid
claims.text: The layer gates the effect pass once on a non-empty grid (all extents above 0 and buffer non-empty), so every effect may assume at least one light on each axis; modifiers still tick.

claims.subject: Layer buffer persistence
claims.text: The layer's buffer persists frame to frame: it is cleared only on allocation and once in prepare, never per frame, so each effect owns its own background and trails are possible.

claims.subject: Layer::fadeToBlackBy
claims.text: Effects request a fade as a rate per 60 Hz reference frame; the layer keeps the gentlest (minimum) request, scales it by elapsed time with a sub-unit carry, and applies one whole-buffer pass at the next frame start.

claims.subject: Layer::tick fade stall
claims.text: A stalled frame is clamped to a fade of 255 and the carry is dropped, so a long idle gap tops up once rather than bursting or banking.

claims.subject: Layer::extrude
claims.text: After each effect tick the layer copies a D1 effect's x=0 column across x and a D1/D2 effect's z=0 slice across z; a D3 effect returns after one comparison.

claims.subject: Layer::blendMode / opacity
claims.text: blendMode and opacity are inert inside the layer; the Drivers container reads them with the child order and composites, and opacity 0 makes the layer neither render nor blend.

claims.subject: Layer::kBlendOps
claims.text: The blend mode enum order, option strings and kBlendOps table must stay aligned (static_assert on the count) so a persisted preset keeps its meaning and an index and its op cannot drift.

claims.subject: Layer::rebuildLUT
claims.text: rebuildLUT first walks the enabled static modifiers in child order to compute the folded logical box via modifyLogicalSize and clampLogical, then chooses identity or a folded LUT.

claims.subject: Layer::rebuildLUT fast path
claims.text: The identity LUT is used only when there is no static modifier, the layout is dense (light count equals box volume), has no gap, and emits lights in box order; otherwise a folded table is built.

claims.subject: Layer::buildFoldedLUT
claims.text: buildFoldedLUT walks the physical lights twice as a compressed sparse row, first counting each logical cell's lights then placing each driver index in its run, folding each coordinate through the static modifier chain in both passes.

claims.subject: Layer::buildFoldedLUT physical-to-logical
claims.text: The build walks physical lights and folds each to a logical cell, so N physical lights folding onto one cell is the fan-out (Multiply kaleidoscope) and the build can never overflow it.

claims.subject: Layer::rebuildLUT degrade
claims.text: If the folded mapping cannot be allocated the layer degrades to identity at the physical size with a warning status instead of crashing, at the cost of lighting a gapped layout.

claims.subject: Layer::allocateBuffer
claims.text: Buffer allocation checks the heap budget and, if the box does not fit, halves each dimension until it does or reaches an 8x8 minimum, reporting 'buffer reduced' or an error status.

claims.subject: Layer::allocateBuffer channels
claims.text: channelsPerLight is widened to cover motion channels before the buffer is allocated, because widening afterwards would resize the buffer under its holder.

claims.subject: Layer::applyLivePass
claims.text: The live pass snapshots the frame into a preallocated scratch and gathers backward: for each destination cell it runs the source coordinate through every live modifier and copies that source cell, or writes black when the source is off-box.

claims.subject: Layer::ensureLiveScratch
claims.text: The live-pass scratch is sized on the cold path and never allocated in the hot path; on allocation failure the pass no-ops and the static frame shows.

claims.subject: Layer::bufferGen
claims.text: bufferGen increments on every write to the shared buffer (fade, each effect, the live pass) so a holder can tell whether the buffer is untouched.

claims.subject: Layer::wiringSource
claims.text: A sender-mapped (wiring-order) frame skips mapping only when the layer is the sole enabled layer, has a LUT, holds exactly one enabled effect and no enabled modifier, and that effect delivers wiring order.

claims.subject: Layer::placeByLayout
claims.text: placeByLayout reads the layout's positions rather than inverting the layer's LUT, because inverting would cancel the static modifiers the frame should still pass through.

claims.subject: effectSetChannel
claims.text: Writing a non-color channel (pan, tilt, zoom, rotate, gobo) is a no-op when the fixture has no such channel, which keeps a moving-head effect harmless on an LED strip.

claims.subject: Effects
claims.text: Effects is the container of layers: it ticks each enabled layer in order, owns no buffer, and answers the compositor's queries (active layer, enabled count, ordered walk).

claims.subject: Effects::tick
claims.text: Effects ticks the scripted palette first so every layer samples the same entries, then ticks each enabled layer, skipping invisible (opacity 0) layers only when more than one layer is enabled.

claims.subject: Effects::prepare / setLayouts
claims.text: If nothing injected a Layouts, Effects finds the top-level one by type from the Scheduler and re-wires every layer child to it, so a layer added through the API is wired too.

claims.subject: Effects::activeLayer vs firstEnabledLayer
claims.text: activeLayer falls back to a disabled layer so geometry stays queryable, while firstEnabledLayer returns null when none is enabled; output selection uses the latter because a disabled layer would keep emitting its last frame.

claims.subject: Effects::forEachEnabledLayer
claims.text: forEachEnabledLayer walks enabled layers bottom to top and flags the first one, which clears the destination so unmapped cells stay black.

claims.subject: Buffer
claims.text: Buffer is the contiguous raw-byte light store, addressed by channel count, so RGB, RGBW and multi-channel DMX fixtures share one type; it is non-copyable and move-only because it owns its allocation.

claims.subject: Buffer::allocate
claims.text: allocate keeps the existing block when asked for the same byte size, only clearing it, so a layer rebuilt every frame at its size takes nothing from the heap.

claims.subject: Buffer locking
claims.text: Buffer patterns stay lock-free (atomic pointer swap or one shared semaphore) because a semaphore costs about 150 bytes on an ESP32.

claims.subject: MappingLUT
claims.text: MappingLUT maps each logical light to zero, one or many physical lights, and needs no table at all on the sequential identity fast path (hasLUT is false).

claims.subject: MappingLUT CSR build
claims.text: The in-place build is count, startRuns, place, endBuild: counts become run starts, place advances a cursor per logical light, and endBuild shifts the cursors back one slot to become the offsets.

claims.subject: MappingLUT::place
claims.text: place is bounded by the destination capacity, so a second pass that disagrees with the first costs a destination, not memory.

claims.subject: MappingLUT paging
claims.text: Destinations split into 4096-entry power-of-two pages when no free block is large enough (and a page index is a shift and mask), because a large map on a no-PSRAM board can outgrow the largest free block and Xtensa has no hardware divide.

claims.subject: MappingLUT::allocateDestinations
claims.text: Destination allocation has three tiers: one block (desktop's unlimited maxAllocBlock always takes it), then pages within the heap budget minus HEAP_RESERVE, then refusal, which frees the table back to identity.

claims.subject: MappingLUT::overwrites
claims.text: overwrites() says every physical destination is written by at most one logical light, which lets blendMap plain-copy (about four times faster) instead of accumulating additively.

claims.subject: MappingLUT::forEachDestination
claims.text: forEachDestination is the hot-path walk of one logical light's physical destinations: identity calls back with the index itself, otherwise it reads offsets[i] to offsets[i+1] from flat or paged storage.

claims.subject: MappingLUT free / beginBuild
claims.text: A failed build or free returns the table to identity mode, and a rebuild at the same size keeps its blocks, so identity is the safe state after any allocation failure.

claims.subject: blendMap
claims.text: blendMap is the one per-layer pass that reads the logical buffer and writes it, mapped and blended, into the physical frame, with a dense memcpy fast path for an identity LUT at full overwrite.

claims.subject: blendMap bounds
claims.text: Every mapped write is bounded by both buffers because a reshape rebuilds the mapping and the output buffer in separate steps, so a render tick can hold new physical indices against the old smaller buffer; the bound prevents heap corruption though that frame may be briefly wrong.

claims.subject: blendMap clearFirst
claims.text: The bottom layer clears the destination before writing so physical cells with no source, such as a sparse layout's gaps, stay black; the identity path needs no clear because it writes every byte.

claims.subject: blendMap Overwrite
claims.text: Overwrite defers to the LUT's overwrites flag, so a folding mapping (several logical lights on one cell) accumulates additively with clamping rather than last-writer-wins.

claims.subject: blendSeparable
claims.text: Blend modes dispatch once per layer to a templated per-mode loop, so each mode gets a tight loop and no per-light mode check, and all math is integer (div255 reciprocal, no division).

claims.subject: BlendOp modes
claims.text: BlendOp offers Overwrite, Alpha, Additive and the W3C separable modes Multiply, Screen, Darken, Lighten, Difference and Exclusion, the latter mixed with the backdrop by opacity as alpha is.

claims.subject: copyChannelsFrom
claims.text: Motion bytes are copied as they are, without opacity, because a motion byte is a position that no fade should scale.

claims.subject: ModifierBase
claims.text: A modifier is a coordinate transform between effect and output that reshapes or masks where pixels land without changing what the effect draws; a layer applies its whole enabled stack in child order.

claims.subject: ModifierBase hooks
claims.text: Three virtual hooks, all no-ops by default, let a modifier implement only what it needs: modifyLogicalSize reshapes the running box, modifyLogical folds one coordinate (false rejects it), and modifyLive remaps per frame.

claims.subject: ModifierBase::modifyLogical
claims.text: modifyLogical returns a bool because a later modulo could alias a sentinel coordinate back into range, so rejection must be explicit.

claims.subject: ModifierBase static vs live
claims.text: A modifier with hasModifyLive true is skipped by the static fold and runs only in the per-frame live pass; every other modifier is baked into the LUT, so a static-only chain costs nothing per frame.

claims.subject: ModifierBase::consumeNeedsRebuild
claims.text: Animated static modifiers (RandomMap) raise a needs-rebuild flag that the layer polls once per frame across all modifiers, so several coalesce into one rebuild that never runs inside a tick.

claims.subject: ModifierBase::prepareScope
claims.text: A modifier's controls rebuild its parent layer only (PrepareScope::Parent), not the whole tree, and Drivers re-prepares only if the layer's shape changed.

claims.subject: ModifierBase::dimensions
claims.text: Unlike an effect's dimensions, a modifier's Dim is advisory only and the layer never extrudes modifier output; it exists for the UI chip.

claims.subject: Modifier chain order
claims.text: Modifier order is meaningful because the chain composes in child order (M1 then M2 ...), so mirror-then-rotate differs from rotate-then-mirror.

claims.subject: clampLogical
claims.text: After every modifier the running box is clamped to at least 1 on each axis that has physical lights, so no modifier can size the layer away to zero.

claims.subject: MirrorModifier
claims.text: MirrorModifier halves each selected axis (rounding up, so an odd extent keeps its unpaired center) and reflects the far half back onto the near half.

claims.subject: MultiplyModifier
claims.text: MultiplyModifier divides the box by a per-axis factor and tiles it with a modulo fold, optionally reflecting every other tile; light past the last whole tile is dropped.

claims.subject: RotateModifier
claims.text: RotateModifier is the one live modifier: it maps backward each frame with an integer inverse rotation matrix about the box center in half-units, so no destination cell is left unfilled.

claims.subject: RotateModifier::tick
claims.text: Rotation angle advances from elapsed time times speed via a raw accumulator, not a per-frame increment, so rotation speed is independent of the render rate and needs no rebuild.

claims.subject: RandomMapModifier
claims.text: RandomMapModifier applies a Fisher-Yates permutation over the box; on each beat its tick bumps a generation and raises needsRebuild, so the layer rebuilds its mapping and the next fold reshuffles.

claims.subject: RandomMapModifier OOM
claims.text: If the permutation cannot be allocated, RandomMap passes coordinates through unchanged, leaving the mapping as it is instead of failing.

claims.subject: RegionModifier
claims.text: RegionModifier crops the layer to a percentage window per axis, using a half-open interval (floored start, ceiled exclusive end) so adjacent windows such as 0-50 and 50-100 neither overlap nor leave a gap.

claims.subject: BlockModifier / CircleModifier
claims.text: BlockModifier and CircleModifier turn a 1D effect into nested rings by folding each light to its Chebyshev (square) or Euclidean (round) distance from the center, with a one-column logical box.

claims.subject: PinwheelModifier
claims.text: PinwheelModifier is a polar fold: atan2 bins each light's angle into a petal on x and its radius becomes the position along the petal, with swirl, symmetry and z-twist bending the pattern.

claims.subject: TransposeModifier
claims.text: TransposeModifier swaps axis pairs in the order XY, XZ, YZ on both box and coordinates so several compose, then applies flips against the already transposed box.

claims.subject: CheckerboardModifier / RippleXZModifier
claims.text: CheckerboardModifier masks the layer by dropping lights on the other-parity squares without resizing the box, and RippleXZModifier collapses chosen axes to a single plane so the effect repeats across them.

claims.subject: light_types.h
claims.text: light_types.h holds the coordinate, count and dimension types (lengthType int16, Coord3D, nrOfLightsType) shared by effects, modifiers, layouts and drivers; it includes the platform layer but never core.

claims.subject: nrOfLightsType
claims.text: nrOfLightsType is 16-bit without PSRAM and 32-bit with it, which halves LUT memory on small devices (24 KB for 12K LEDs) while letting large HUB75 panels exceed 65K.

claims.subject: Coord3D operators
claims.text: Coord3D's % and / guard a non-positive divisor by returning the dividend unchanged, so a modifier folds a zero-extent axis without pre-checking it.

claims.subject: lengthType
claims.text: lengthType is a signed 16-bit coordinate because a byte is too narrow for a 128-edge grid and effects may address out-of-bounds negative positions.

claims.subject: FixtureChannels
claims.text: FixtureChannels names which byte offsets inside a layer light carry pan, tilt, zoom, rotate and gobo; absent roles are kAbsent (255) and their setters are no-ops.

claims.subject: FixtureChannels color offset
claims.text: Color is always at offset 0 of a layer light and motion channels pack after it from slot 4 in a fixed order; these layer slots differ from the fixture's own offsets, which Correction::apply translates on output.

claims.subject: Palette
claims.text: A Palette is sixteen evenly spaced RGB entries; a gradient stop list in flash is expanded into them once on selection, off the hot path, so the per-light lookup is a single blend.

claims.subject: colorFromPalette
claims.text: colorFromPalette uses the index's high nibble to pick the entry and the low nibble times 17 as the blend toward the next entry, wrapping 15 to 0.

claims.subject: ArtNetPacket / DdpPacket / E131Packet
claims.text: Each network wire format lives in one header shared by sender and receiver so the two cannot drift, with unit tests round-tripping build against parse.

claims.subject: DDP_MAX_PAYLOAD
claims.text: DDP carries 480 RGB lights a packet against Art-Net's 170 because per-packet cost dominates wire time, and its 1440-byte payload is divisible by both 3 and 4.

claims.subject: FseqFile
claims.text: FseqFile.h is a pure parser of the FSEQ sequence header, compression flags and sparse-range table with no platform calls or I/O, reading only caller-supplied buffers and never past len.

claims.subject: RtpH264 Packetiser
claims.text: The RTP H.264 packetiser sends a NAL that fits alone as one packet and fragments larger ones into FU-A packets, with the marker bit on the last packet of a frame and one shared timestamp per frame.

claims.subject: RtspSession
claims.text: A client's Transport header is judged one comma-separated alternative at a time and the first usable one (RTP/AVP, unicast, with a port) wins, to avoid mixing the protocol of one alternative with the port of another.

notes: Skipped line-level reading of the full Palette built-in gradient tables, FseqFile expandSparseFrame and block validation, ArtNet/E131 poll-reply internals, RtspSession verb handling and the bodies of Cube, HumanSizedCube, CarLights, Rings241, TorontoBarGourds, Spiral and Ring placement math; their claims rest on class headers and a few read bodies. docs/moonmodules/light/supporting.md is a 3-line stub with no technical content in scope. The doc-home claims about Layer.cpp-level lifecycle (applyState recursion order) are in core and not verified here. Doc home for pipe-056 and 057 cites the frames-from-outside section; I did not verify Drivers-side use of wiringSource.
